Hi Sam — thanks for the concise list. Short answers up front, then a few specifics and the artifacts attached.

1) Regions: By default, hosted API traffic for US customers is handled in US regions (primary execution in us-west-2 or us-east-1). For customers who require EU-only processing we offer EU-hosted tenant options (europe-west1 / eu-central1) and can pin routes to those regions.

2) Subprocessors: For the hosted API the primary subprocessors that may process request payloads or logs are: AWS (EC2, S3) for model execution and artifact storage; Google Cloud (optional EU buckets for customers who choose EU-hosted tenant); Cloudflare (edge routing and caching of small artifacts); Datadog (telemetry, traces) — telemetry is pseudonymized by default; Sentry (error payloads — can be disabled); and HashiCorp Vault (key wrapping for customer keys). For dedicated or private deployments we limit third-party exposure per contract (details below).

3) Cross-border transfers: Hosted backups and analytics aggregates may replicate to secondary zones for durability and monitoring. If you select US-hosted tenant we will not intentionally route inference payloads to non-US execution regions; however transient routing (egress through a CDN edge or temporary replicas for cache warmup) can touch secondary locations for short durations. Backups for logs/metrics are retained according to the retention table in the attached processing map (redwood-processing-map.pdf).

Evidence attached: redwood-processing-map.pdf (high-level hop map) and a draft SOW that outlines region controls and a timeline for locking a tenant to a region.

- I'll loop Legal with a subprocessor appendix and SOC2 pointer.
- If HealthQA needs an EU-only execution promise we can scope an EU-hosted tenant (timeline ~2–3 weeks to provision sandbox).

I'll add Jonas and Marissa on the legal/ops specifics.

Hi Sam — quick operational clarifications from the ops side:

- Ephemeral data: During inference we keep a short-lived KV cache in memory (no persistent disk) to accelerate long-running chats. That cache is erased on instance termination (typical TTL seconds-to-minutes) and is not written to object storage.
- Logs vs. payloads: Detailed request payloads are only written to object storage if you enable request-level logging for debugging. By default we store only metadata (token counts, latency, error codes) and a truncated prompt hash for quality telemetry.
- Backups: Model artifacts are replicated across two AZs within the tenant region; control plane data (customer workspace configs) is stored in a region-specific database and replicated per your tenant selection. Archived logs may be encrypted and moved to long-term storage (S3 Glacier equivalent) — retention aligns with your contract.

If you want, we can provide a minimal test tenant with regional locking and logging disabled so your security team can run a few requests and verify no data leaves the region.

Marissa
